name: Ironclad Agrisystems Fungal Spore Relay
description:
Originally developed for coordinating sensor networks across Ironclad's vast agri-industrial growing facilities, the Fungal Spore Relay is a biological mesh networking system that propagates communication nodes through the dispersal of engineered fungal spores. Each spore carries a dormant piezoelectric transmitter lattice — microscopic, printed directly onto the spore's outer membrane — that activates upon contact with a moisture-rich surface and begins exchanging encrypted handshake signals with nearby activated spores. A sufficiently dense spore cloud, dispersed through a target area, self-organizes into a low-bandwidth mesh network within four to eight hours of dispersal.

The system was designed for Ironclad's agricultural monitoring applications, where running physical cable across hundreds of hectares is impractical. Its adaptation for urban use in GLMZ was not officially sanctioned. The spores, dispersed from a canister roughly the size of a thermos, are effectively invisible once airborne and leave no obvious physical trace — they settle into wall surfaces, ventilation systems, and organic material, making network removal nearly impossible without chemical treatment of the entire affected area. The mesh degrades naturally over approximately three weeks as the spore membranes break down.

Ironclad has issued multiple public statements distancing itself from the device's use in urban surveillance and covert communications, but the black market modification kits that adapt agricultural canisters for urban dispersal are manufactured in GLMZ's industrial districts using Ironclad's own spore stock, diverted from legitimate supply chains. The company's attempts to introduce a sterility kill-switch into the spore production line have been undermined repeatedly by employees on the take.

specifications.dispersal_range: Standard canister covers approximately 1,500 square meters in still air; reduced in high ventilation
specifications.network_formation_time: 4–8 hours post-dispersal for minimum viable mesh density
specifications.network_bandwidth: Very low — text and short compressed audio only
specifications.mesh_lifespan: Approximately 18–22 days before substrate degradation renders network unreliable
specifications.removal_method: Chemical treatment (Ironclad industrial fungicide, or equivalent); physical removal impractical
specifications.detection: Spores individually undetectable by standard scanners; network traffic detectable by specialized bio-EM analysis equipment

tactical_use: Deployed covertly into a target area — through ventilation systems, open windows, or simply carried through a space — to establish a persistent, infrastructure-independent mesh network that survives even if all conventional comms in the area are jammed or shut down. Useful for establishing communication in occupied or locked-down zones. The three-week lifespan means it functions as a temporary operational network that self-destructs without leaving hardware evidence.
cultural_context: The Fungal Spore Relay has become notorious in GLMZ after several high-profile incidents in which entire corporate office blocks were found to be hosting active biological mesh networks of unknown origin. The incidents sparked a minor public panic about biological surveillance, which Ironclad handled with aggressive PR positioning as a victim of supply-chain theft. In underground communities, 'blooming a building' has entered the lexicon as a verb meaning to seed a space with persistent covert infrastructure.
known_users: Urban insurgent cells requiring persistent infrastructure in contested zones
Investigative journalists establishing secure channels inside monitored facilities
Rival corporate intelligence teams conducting long-duration passive surveillance
story_hooks: A corporate client hires the players to find and eliminate a Fungal Relay network inside their headquarters — three weeks of internal communications may have been harvested, and they don't know by whom.
A player unknowingly carries a pre-seeded canister through a secure facility; the network that forms is traced back to them.

Ironclad Agrisystems quietly offers a contract: recover the modification kit schematics from the black market manufacturer before a regulatory investigation forces Ironclad to admit how thoroughly their supply chain has been compromised.

A building the players are operating out of begins showing signs of an active Fungal Relay network that predates their arrival — someone seeded it before them, and the mesh is still transmitting to an unknown receiver.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, cylindrical pressurized canister resembling a high-end thermos or industrial aerosol dispenser. The body tapers slightly toward a precision-engineered dispersal nozzle at the apex. Deliberately utilitarian and unmarked to avoid attention in urban environments.
physical_description.dimensions: 28cm tall, 8cm diameter — fits comfortably in a jacket pocket or small carrypack when wrapped
physical_description.weight_description: Handheld, roughly 400–500 grams when full; lightweight enough for single-hand operation or concealment
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade aluminum alloy with internal ceramic pressure vessel; aerospace safety seals
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with subtle brushed texture to minimize reflectivity; minimal branding to avoid detection
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with anodized dark bronze accent bands near the nozzle and base; pressure gauge window shows faint amber-orange indicator fluid
physical_description.interface_elements: Single-stage trigger mechanism at the base (ambidextrous grip), transparent pressure gauge window (0–300 PSI scale), micro-LED status indicator (dormant until armed), threaded pressure-relief valve cap, stealth-mode passive safety lock
distinctive_features: Ultra-fine precision dispersal nozzle with internal baffle designed to create near-silent, barely-visible aerosol cloud
Micro-etched serial numbers (deliberately worn/obscured on black-market units)
Pressure gauge dial with dual-language markings (English/Mandarin — origin trace)
Faint bioluminescent tinting visible on internal spore payload when backlit (engineered marker for agricultural tracking, difficult to remove)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: IRONCLAD AGRISYSTEMS logo (subtle, often removed or defaced on black-market canisters); model designation 'FSR-7' stamped on the base; legitimate units carry USDA/GLMZ regulatory stamps (absent on diverted stock)
physical_description.condition_typical: Black-market units show signs of hasty modification: tape-wrapped seams, scratched logos, aftermarket pressure-relief modifications, sometimes spray-painted matte to further obscure branding; legitimate agricultural units appear pristine and heavily labeled
